Subject: Request: topology, isolation, and evidence for SOC 2 intake

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we start our SOC 2 scoping with Verdant's audit team, they asked for a compact security architecture bundle that covers network-level isolation for Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically they're looking for: 

- A single-page topology diagram that highlights control-plane vs data-plane boundaries for both Dedicated and Private options.
- A short matrix mapping tenant isolation controls (VPC boundaries, subnet zoning, egress controls) to SIG/CAT control IDs.
- Any artifact that demonstrates operational enforcement (firewall rules, routing policies, or KMS boundary notes).

Can you package something concise (1–3 pages + a matrix) we can include in the auditor intake? We prefer a single archive or drive link.

Appreciate it — the deadline from audit is tight (Nov 19).

Best,
Marina
Security Program Manager
Verdant Analytics

Marina —

Thanks for the clear ask. I've put together a compact bundle for the auditor and attached the primary artifacts below:

1) guardrail-topology-v1.png — single-page diagram showing control-plane (management) vs data-plane (inference traffic) boundaries for Hosted / Dedicated / Private, with notes on routing and NAT egress points.
2) isolation-validation-matrix.xlsx — a short mapping of SIG control families to our enforcement points (network ACLs, perimeter firewalls, service-level RBAC, KMS scope).
3) soc2-evidence-index.pdf — index of logs, runbooks, and sample configs (redacted) with pointers to the Drive folder.

A few implementation notes up-front so the auditor has context:
- Dedicated: customer workloads run in a reserved GPU pool; control plane is shared but logically segmented via mutual TLS + service identity tokens. Egress from the Dedicated work nodes is via customer-segregated NATs and per-tenant egress policies.
- Private (VPC): the control plane can be customer-managed or hosted with a private peering; data-plane traffic remains inside customer VPCs where requested, and we support an optional air-gapped bundle for on-prem installations.
- Enforcement: we use prefix-based routing + firewall policy templates applied by orchestration; KV caches and model artifacts are stored in per-tenant encrypted buckets with KMS key scoping.

We tried to keep the diagram and matrix auditor-friendly. If you want, Kimberly can add a couple of annotated snapshots of actual firewall rule snapshots and a short note tying each matrix row back to a SIG/CAT id.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XyZ-ExampleDriveLink (pack v1)

I'll leave Kimberly and Karthik on-thread for the technical attachments.

— Jonas

Redwood Inference

> - Dedicated: customer workloads run in a reserved GPU pool; control plane is shared but logically segmented via mutual TLS + service identity tokens. Egress from the Dedicated work nodes is via customer-segregated NATs and per-tenant egress policies.
> - Private (VPC): the control plane can be customer-managed or hosted with a private peering; data-plane traffic remains inside customer VPCs where requested, and we support an optional air-gapped bundle for on-prem installations.

Adding a couple of clarifications to make the auditer's mapping straightforward:

- Tenant fencing: we implement a three-layer separation model 
  * Network layer: per-tenant subnets + route tables; management plane endpoints are reachable only over mTLS-authenticated control channels and are filtered by source identity.
  * Compute layer: container runtime namespaces and GPU isolation via cgroup policies and slot allocation.
  * Storage layer: per-tenant encrypted object stores (SSE-KMS), bucket policies scoped to tenant service identity.

- Egress controls: we provide both centralized egress gateways (for Hosted/Dedicated) and a route-only model for Private (customer-managed). The matrix includes sample ACL lines and a Jinja template we use for audit snapshots.

- Evidence items: I've redacted IPs in the PDF but included exemplar firewall rule excerpts and the KMS key policy snippet (policy ids masked). If the auditor needs unredacted configs, we can provide them under an NDA and timebox.

If this layout works for Verdant's auditor, we can finalize and generate a small one-page cover note linking each matrix row to the canonical SIG and CAIQ control IDs (I'll draft that).

Thanks — Kim
Principal Security Architect
Redwood Inference
